translation.notice: Translation for reference; the English version is official.
voice.heard: We heard you. Check the words, change them if you like, then send.
voice.denied: The microphone is blocked. Allow microphone access in your browser settings, or type your answer.
voice.unsupported: This browser cannot listen to your voice. Type your answer instead.
voice.nothingHeard: We did not hear anything. Try again, or type your answer.
voice.noMicrophone: No microphone was found. Type your answer instead.
voice.error: Listening did not work this time. Try again, or type your answer.
audio.deviceVoice: Device voice: the voice installed on your phone or computer.
audio.unavailable: This browser cannot read aloud. Read the text on the screen.
compare.legend: Dashed words are missing from your answer. Crossed-out words were extra.
intro.notice.practice: This is a practice tool only.
intro.notice.government: It is not a government service and is not affiliated with USCIS.
intro.privacy: Do not say your real name, address, date of birth or A-number. Practice as the fictional profile you choose.
intro.filed.legend: Practice as if the N-400 was filed…
intro.filed.help: This decides whether you practice the 2008 or the 2025 civics test. It is only a practice choice. For your own case, check uscis.gov to see which test applies to you.
intro.startHint: Make your choice above to start.
intro.locked: Civics scoring is switched off in this build until a person has reviewed the answer key. You can still practice the interview, reading and writing.
n400.title: N-400 interview
n400.lead: A calm run through the kind of questions an officer asks about an application. Answer as {name}. Nothing in this step is scored.
n400.sample.label: Sample answer for {name} (fictional)
n400.sample.note: This is only the made-up profile’s answer. In a real interview you answer truthfully about your own life.
n400.failed: The next question could not be loaded. Start over to try again.
n400.done.title: Your answers
n400.done.lead: These are the words you gave. They are not scored.
voice.privacy: Voice uses your browser’s speech recognition. Depending on your browser, your voice may be processed by the browser’s maker. Language Lab does not record or send your voice, and nothing is saved when you close this page.
reading.title: Reading
reading.lead: Read the sentence out loud. You can type it if you prefer.
reading.done.passed: You read a sentence correctly. Reading is done.
reading.done.notPassed: That was the last sentence. More practice will help.
writing.title: Writing
writing.lead: Listen to the sentence, then type it.
writing.sentence: Listen, then type what you hear
writing.done.passed: You wrote a sentence correctly. Writing is done.
writing.done.notPassed: That was the last sentence. More practice will help.
compare.notYet: Not yet: {percent}% of the words matched.
compare.setting: Practice setting: at least {percent}% of the words must match. This is a Language Lab setting, not a USCIS rule.
compare.vocab: The sentences use only words from the official USCIS reading and writing vocabulary lists.
writing.fallback: This browser cannot read aloud, so the sentence is shown here. Type it.
writing.hidden: The sentence stays hidden until you answer.
civics.title: Civics
civics.lead: Answer out loud or type. Short answers are fine, but say the whole answer.
civics.officialNote: Any of these counts. The list is taken from the USCIS answer list and is still waiting for a person to review it.
civics.stopped.correct: You reached the practice passing score, so the test stopped here.
civics.stopped.incorrect: The test stopped because too many answers need more practice.
civics.stopped.none: You have answered every question for this practice test.
civics.locked.title: Civics is switched off in this build
civics.locked.text: The civics answer key is still waiting for a person to review it, so this build does not score civics or make a report.
report.n400Note: The N-400 interview is practice only and is not scored.
voice.needText: Type or say your answer first, or choose Skip.
audio.aiVoice: AI-generated voice. The audio was made ahead of time.
home.title: Welcome to the booth
home.lead: Practice for the naturalization interview in a quiet booth. You answer as a made-up person, so you don't need to share real details.
home.how.title: How it works
home.how.1.title: Listen
home.how.1.text: Tap Play aloud to hear a question or a sentence.
home.how.2.title: Speak or type
home.how.2.text: Say your answer, or type it. Typing always works.
home.how.3.title: See the result
home.how.3.text: You see how your answer compares, and what to practice next.
home.choose: What would you like to do?
home.full.title: Full practice interview
home.full.text: All four parts in order, then one report.
home.parts.title: Practice one part
home.part.n400.title: N-400 interview
home.part.n400.text: Answer questions about an application. Not scored.
home.part.reading.title: Reading
home.part.writing.title: Writing
home.part.civics.title: Civics
home.part.civics.text: Answer civics questions. Checked against the answer key.
setup.title: Set up your practice
setup.lead: Choose what this practice needs. Nothing real is asked.
disclaimer.report: This is a practice tool only. It is not affiliated with USCIS or any government agency. Results do not predict or reflect any official immigration decision. This is not legal advice.
partReport.scope: This report is for one part only. It shows how this part went in practice, not how you would do on the real test, and it gives no overall practice result.
partReport.n400.lead: These are your own words. This part is not scored.
partReport.none: Nothing was answered in this part.
partReport.unscored.title: Not scored
partReport.unscored.text: These questions could not be scored, so they are not counted as right or wrong.
partReport.unscored.missing: A question that is not in the answer key
help.setup.1: Tap one choice in each group on this screen.
help.setup.2: Profiles are made up. Do not type your real name or any details about you.
help.listen: Press “{play}” to hear it. Press the same button again to stop.
help.sample: Read the sample answer, or play it. It belongs to the made-up person. It is only an example.
help.read: Read the sentence on the screen out loud.
help.mic: Press “{say}” and speak. If your phone asks to use the microphone, press Allow. Press “{stop}” when you finish.
help.type: You can always type instead. Tap the box and type. Typing always works.
help.typeOnly: Tap the box and type what you hear.
help.send: Check the words in the box. You can change them. Then press “{send}”.
help.skip: Press “{skip}” if you do not know. It sends an empty answer and moves on. It counts as not yet.
help.notScored: Nothing in this part is scored.
help.result.reading: Then you see which words matched.
help.result.civics: Then you see Correct or Not yet, and the official answers.
settings.title: Comfort settings
settings.slow.label: Play recorded voices more slowly
settings.slow.help: This only changes the speed. It is the same recording.
settings.memory: These settings last until you close or reload this page.
lang.label: Language
lang.interviewEnglish: The real interview is held in English unless USCIS allows an exception for you. The questions and sentences on these screens stay in English so you can practice them.
header.homeConfirm: Go back to home? Your answers in this practice will be lost.
aiNotice.text: This translation was made by AI and may contain mistakes. The English version is the authoritative one.
lang.menu.title: Choose a language
home.study.title: Study first
home.study.text: Look through the civics questions with pictures and the official answers. Nothing is scored.
study.lead: Look through the civics questions one at a time. Each one shows the official answers. Nothing is scored or saved.
study.version.legend: Which civics test do you want to study?
study.locked: Study first is switched off in this build until a person has reviewed the answer key.
credits.title: Picture credits
credits.lead: The pictures in civics practice come from official U.S. federal sources. Each one is used only because its own record states its rights. This does not mean any agency endorses Language Lab.
